top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Majka Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.

Road-specific control matters at Majka Gran Fondo. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 53 miles.
93ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
At Majka Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Majka Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
53 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Majka Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Low-cadence force work supports 4,954ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 4,954ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
